data.text: Comprehensive guide to using Retrieval-Augmented Generation (RAG) and AI features in LLM Notetaker.
Retrieval-Augmented Generation (RAG) combines the power of large language models with your specific documents to provide accurate, grounded responses.
RAG allows the AI to answer questions based on your uploaded documents rather than just its training data, ensuring responses are relevant and factual.
data.caption: Key Concept

items: Document Upload: You upload PDFs, DOCX, or CSV files to a chat
Text Extraction: The system extracts and processes text from your documents
Vectorization: Document content is converted to mathematical vectors (embeddings)
Storage: Vectors are stored in ChromaDB for efficient similarity search
Query Processing: When you ask a question, it's also converted to a vector
Retrieval: The system finds the most relevant document sections
Generation: AI generates responses using both the question and relevant context
Quality Matters: Use clear, well-formatted documents for best results
Size Considerations: Larger documents work well, but very large files may need chunking
Multiple Sources: Upload related documents together for comprehensive coverage
Clean Text: Avoid heavily image-based PDFs or corrupted files
Be Specific: Ask targeted questions rather than very broad ones
Reference Context: Mention specific sections or topics when relevant
Follow Up: Build on previous answers to dive deeper into topics
Request Sources: Ask for specific page numbers or section references

data.code:
# Example effective questions:

# ✅ Good questions:
"What are the performance metrics for ResNet mentioned in the paper?"
"Compare the methodologies used in sections 3.1 and 3.2"
"What limitations does the author mention for this approach?"

# ❌ Less effective:
"Tell me about this document"
"What's in here?"
"Summarize everything"

data.text: Understanding the AI models and their capabilities helps you use them effectively:

items: Upload multiple research papers on a topic
Ask for comparisons between different studies
Extract key findings and methodologies
Identify gaps in the research
Generate literature review summaries
Upload contracts or legal documents
Ask about specific clauses or terms
Identify potential issues or inconsistencies
Compare different versions of documents
Extract action items and deadlines
Upload CSV files with structured data
Ask questions about trends and patterns
Get explanations of data relationships
Identify outliers or anomalies
Generate insights for decision-making
Token Limits: Very long documents may be truncated or chunked
Context Window: AI has limited memory of very long conversations
Accuracy: Always verify critical information from original sources
Privacy: Be mindful of sensitive information in uploaded documents
Processing Time: Large documents may take longer to process initially
